title: The Sixteen Commandments
content_zh:
The Sixteen Commandments of Sun Tzu on the Conduct of Officers:
1. The general must be wise and perceptive.
2. He must be sincere and trustworthy.
3. He must be benevolent and love his men.
4. He must be courageous and decisive.
5. He must be strict in maintaining discipline.
6. Terrain is the general's greatest ally.
7. He who occupies the high ground first fights with ease.
8. Speed is the essence of war.
9. Exploit the enemy's lack of preparation.
10. Strike where the enemy least expects.
11. The value of time — that is, being a little ahead of your opponent.
12. Often counts for more than either superior numbers or greater resources.
13. There are roads not to follow.
14. There are armies not to be attacked.
15. There are towns not to be besieged.
16. There are positions not to be contested.
